title: A Practical Guide to Consultant Professional Liability Insurance

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.purpose: Address the 'Introduction' requirement from the approved content strategy without introducing unsupported claims.
sections.body: The Hartford's consultant guidance frames professional liability insurance as coverage relevant to consultants who provide services directly to customers and face claims involving errors, omissions, negligence, misrepresentation, or inaccurate advice.

sections.heading: What You Need to Know
sections.purpose: Address the 'What You Need to Know' requirement from the approved content strategy without introducing unsupported claims.
sections.body:
The Hartford explains that professional liability insurance can help protect a business when a client claims that a mistake in professional services caused a financial loss. It identifies negligence, misrepresentation, and inaccurate advice as examples of claims.

Hiscox describes professional liability insurance, also called errors and omissions insurance, as protection for businesses sued over negligent performance of professional services and recommends it for businesses that provide professional services or regularly give advice to clients.

The Hartford says consultants who provide services directly to customers should consider professional liability insurance and describes common consultant claims involving errors, omissions, negligence, misrepresentation, and inaccurate advice.

sections.heading: Coverage and Key Factors

Cornell's risk guidance says professional liability coverage for consultants can address claims involving negligence, personal injury such as libel and slander, work completed in the past, and employees or independent contractors

sections.heading: Costs and Pricing Factors
sections.purpose: Address the 'Costs and Pricing Factors' requirement from the approved content strategy without introducing unsupported claims.
sections.body:
Insureon reports that consultants pay an average of $62 per month for professional liability insurance, with annual policy costs ranging from around $400 to over $3,750. It says the figures are based on the median cost of policies purchased by consulting businesses through Insureon.

The Hartford says professional liability insurance costs for consultants vary by business and lists claims history, type of business, coverage limits, and experience as factors that can affect the cost.

Insureon says the cost of professional liability insurance depends on factors including the services offered, revenue, coverage limits, and other business risks.

sections.heading: How to Compare Options
sections.purpose: Address the 'How to Compare Options' requirement from the approved content strategy without introducing unsupported claims.
sections.body:
Insureon says consultants comparing professional liability policies should review the coverage limits, deductible, and exclusions because policies can provide different types and amounts of coverage.

The Hartford explains that many professional liability policies are claims-made and that a retroactive date and extended reporting period affect when claims can be covered; it recommends understanding these terms when evaluating a policy.

Insureon says professional liability policies can differ in the types and amounts of coverage they provide and advises reviewing policy language for claims-made versus occurrence coverage, coverage limits, deductibles, and exclusions.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.purpose: Address the 'Frequently Asked Questions' requirement from the approved content strategy without introducing unsupported claims.
sections.body:
How does professional liability insurance work?: The Hartford explains that professional liability insurance, also called E&O insurance, can protect a business when a client claims that a mistake in professional services caused financial loss; it also explains that many professional liability policies are claims-made and that occurrence policies can cover losses that happen during the policy period even if reported after expiration.

What does professional liability insurance cover?: The Hartford says professional liability insurance can help cover errors and omissions, personal injury, misrepresentation, negligence, and inaccurate advice, and can also help pay legal defense costs, disciplinary proceedings, loss of earnings, damages, and subpoena assistance.

Who needs professional liability insurance?: The Hartford says businesses that provide services directly to customers or regularly give advice to clients should consider professional liability insurance, and consultants are specifically included in its industry guidance.

Do consultants need professional liability insurance?: Insureon says businesses that offer professional services or give advice to clients need professional liability insurance, and specifically identifies consultants among businesses that should secure coverage against negligence, errors, or failure to perform services.
